problem: "It is cheap and correct for a true flat face" is too strong. Flat shading uses one normal and one light vector for the whole face; with a nearby point light, and with a perspective viewer, both L and V change from point to point, so even a planar face is not uniformly lit.
fix: Say it is exact only when L and V are effectively constant over the face, that is a directional light seen with an orthographic (or very distant) viewer; with a close point light even a flat face shows a brightness variation that flat shading cannot show.

problem: The trap "Thinking n changes brightness" can mislead. Raising n lowers (R·V)ⁿ for every R·V < 1, so the specular term away from the mirror direction does get dimmer as n grows. Only the peak value at R·V = 1 is set by ks alone.
fix: State it as: ks sets the peak highlight value (at R·V = 1); n sets how quickly the highlight falls off, so a larger n gives a narrower highlight and a smaller value at any fixed off-axis R·V.

where: Section 2, first sentence after the formula legend
problem: "Use max(0, N·L) and max(0, R·V)" repeats the same instruction already given at the end of the legend line, so the reader meets the clamp rule twice in a row.
fix: Keep the clamp instruction once, in the legend, and start the paragraph with "If N·L is negative the light is behind the surface and contributes no diffuse term."

problem: "Physically based rendering replaces the three coefficients with material roughness and metalness" leaves out the base colour. PBR materials normally carry base colour (albedo) as well, which is what replaces kd in practice.
fix: Write: "Physically based rendering replaces ka, kd and ks with a base colour (albedo), a roughness and a metalness per material."
